open_points.subject: A9 deployment admission
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
open_points.question: Must every deployment be admitted only through this route, and what prevents a manual or alternative deployment from bypassing the check?
options: The route is the exclusive deployment gate and bypass is impossible or refused.
The route is the supported path, but other deployment paths may exist if they perform an equivalent check.
The route merely provides the check and operational procedure must ensure it is used.
open_points.default_guess: Make the route the exclusive deployment gate.

witness.initial: A deployment image contains a PyPI distribution with a known vulnerability, and the ordinary route would refuse it.
events: An operator deploys the image through an alternative or manual path that does not invoke the route check.
outcomes: The deployment is refused because every deployment must pass through the exclusive route.
The deployment proceeds because only deployments using the named route are checked.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of the deployed service

open_points.subject: A9 deployment route
open_points.text: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's
open_points.question: Is this the same Factory deployment route used by the Client Portal, a separate route implementing the same policy, or the service's HTTPS route mentioned by R0-16?
options: The service and Client Portal share one Factory deployment route.
The service has a separate deployment route with the same policy as the Client Portal.
This refers to the HTTPS request route through the Portal front.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a separate service deployment pipeline governed by the same policy as the Client Portal.

open_points.subject: A9 dependency check implementation
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built
open_points.question: What built component performs the check, obtains the installed-distribution inventory and OSV snapshot, evaluates OSV records, and returns the admission decision?
options: A named Factory gate and its declared policy reader perform it.
A named third-party vulnerability scanner performs it with specified arguments and result semantics.
A service-specific deployment script implements it.
open_points.default_guess: Use a named Factory deployment gate with explicitly declared inputs and result semantics.

open_points.subject: A9 OSV snapshot freshness
open_points.text: that the deployment route accepts as current. That route owns the age limit
open_points.question: What is the maximum accepted snapshot age, and from which timestamp is its age measured?
options: A fixed maximum age stated in State 2, measured from the snapshot's authoritative creation timestamp.
A deployment configuration value with a named field and unit.
A policy value owned by the Factory route and supplied through a declared gate policy.
open_points.default_guess: Use a Factory-owned declared policy value measured from the snapshot creation timestamp.

witness.initial: The available OSV snapshot was created 36 hours before deployment and the scan otherwise completes successfully with no findings.
events: The deployment route evaluates whether the snapshot is current.
outcomes: A 24-hour limit makes the route refuse the deployment.
A 48-hour limit makes the route admit the deployment.

open_points.subject: A9 freshness time
open_points.text: Before each deployment every distribution installed in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts as current.
open_points.question: What source supplies the current instant for the freshness comparison, in what representation and time zone is it compared with the snapshot timestamp, and how many readings are taken for one deployment?
options: Read an injected system clock once per deployment and compare aware UTC instants.
Use the deployment host wall clock, potentially reading it for each check.
Use an instant supplied by the Factory deployment authority.
open_points.default_guess: Read one authoritative aware-UTC instant from the deployment authority for the whole deployment.

witness.initial: A snapshot is exactly at the permitted age boundary while the wall clock changes during a scan.
events: The route starts checking the image.
The route evaluates snapshot freshness before or during checks of multiple distributions.
outcomes: One captured instant makes the snapshot current for the entire deployment.
Repeated clock reads make early checks current but a later check stale, refusing the deployment.

open_points.subject: A9 check failure
open_points.text: a check that cannot complete does not pass
open_points.question: Exactly which conditions mean that the check cannot complete, and what result must each produce?
options: Any scanner error, unreadable or malformed snapshot, incomplete package inventory, unsupported package metadata, timeout, or indeterminate OSV match refuses deployment.
Only failure of the scanning process itself refuses; individual uncheckable distributions are ignored.
Each failure class has an explicit closed mapping to refusal or successful completion.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every indeterminate inventory, database, scanner, or matching condition as a deployment refusal.

witness.initial: The image contains one installed distribution whose version metadata the checker cannot parse; all other distributions have no findings.
events: The deployment route inventories the image and attempts the OSV check.
outcomes: The deployment is refused because the image could not be checked completely.
The uncheckable distribution is skipped and the deployment is admitted because the scanner process completed.

open_points.subject: A9 deployment occurrence
open_points.question: Which events count as a deployment requiring a new check: initial release, update, rollback, replica creation, restart, or redeployment of an unchanged digest?
options: Every admission or rollout event, including rollback and redeployment, requires a fresh current-snapshot check.
Only creation of a new deployment image requires the check; reuse of the same digest reuses its result.
A check result may be reused for a stated period tied to an immutable image digest.
open_points.default_guess: Require a fresh check for every rollout or rollback admission event.

open_points.subject: INV-15
open_points.text: INV-15: no distribution with a known vulnerability is deployed.
open_points.question: Does INV-15 also require a complete check against an acceptably current snapshot before deployment, or must completeness and freshness be separate formal invariants?
options: Expand INV-15 to state vulnerability absence, snapshot freshness, complete inventory, and fail-closed checking.
Keep INV-15 for vulnerability findings and add separate invariants for freshness and check completion.
Treat freshness and completion as non-invariant deployment procedure.
open_points.default_guess: Add separate formal invariants for current-snapshot use and fail-closed completion.

open_points.subject: INV-15 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-15: the deployment route refuses an image holding a distribution with a known vulnerability, and refuses when the check cannot complete.
open_points.question: What Required tests item demonstrates that a stale or otherwise unaccepted OSV snapshot cannot admit an image, and that every installed PyPI distribution is included in the check?
options: Extend this item with stale-snapshot and omitted-distribution cases.
Add separate Required tests items for freshness and complete inventory.
Declare that the existing witness already asserts these cases and name them explicitly on the line.
open_points.default_guess: Add separate Required tests items with named witnesses for freshness and complete inventory.

witness.initial: An image has two installed PyPI distributions; the route scans only one against a stale snapshot and finds no vulnerability.
events: The deployment route reports that its invoked scan completed successfully.
outcomes: The deployment is refused because the snapshot is not current and the inventory was incomplete.
The deployment is admitted because the stated Required tests only require refusal for a reported vulnerability or a check that reports it could not complete.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and security reviewer
